environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: With cache_bytes=200000, each filler /api/x?vN? fetches once and is cached; after six fillers the original /api/x?<smug> victim fetches upstream again (hit 10, captured upstream line proves the miss) and after twelve it misses again (hit 16). The poison survives only while it is the sole or least-recently-used entry; persistence across real traffic pressure is negative on all four builds.
findings.title: Poison does not survive ordinary cache pressure: six distinct targets evict it

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
Raw client bytes and raw upstream bytes captured in hex
Payload diffed against the control line
